expected: http:// redirects to https:// on the same registrable domain with permanent redirects (301 or 308), at most 5 hops.
limitations: Starts at http://host/ only; other hosts, paths, and ports are not tested.
One request from one network vantage point; other regions, clients, and times can differ.

expected: The TLS handshake to https://host/ succeeds with a certificate chain that verifies.
limitations: Default client verification only: no revocation, expiry-horizon, key-strength, or protocol-version analysis.
One request from one network vantage point; other regions, clients, and times can differ.

expected: strict-transport-security with max-age of at least 31536000 seconds.
limitations: Reads the header on one https response; does not check subdomains.
One request from one network vantage point; other regions, clients, and times can differ.

expected: strict-transport-security includes both includeSubDomains and preload.
limitations: Does not consult the Chromium HSTS preload list, so it cannot say the domain is preloaded. The list holds individual .gov domains (thousands, not every one) and has no entry for the .gov or .mil top-level domains, so a missing preload token here does not show the domain is unprotected; check hstspreload.org.
One request from one network vantage point; other regions, clients, and times can differ.

expected: Exactly one v=spf1 record at the apex that ends in -all or ~all.
limitations: Does not evaluate include chains or lookup limits, and cannot tell whether the domain sends mail.
One request from one network vantage point; other regions, clients, and times can differ.

expected: A v=DMARC1 record at _dmarc.<apex> with p=reject.
limitations: Does not check rua/ruf reporting, subdomain policy, alignment, or whether mail actually authenticates.
One request from one network vantage point; other regions, clients, and times can differ.

expected: /vulnerability-disclosure-policy returns 200 with text (the BOD 20-01 obligation); /.well-known/security.txt is recommended.
limitations: Checks that a policy page and a security.txt exist, not that the policy is adequate, current, or answered.
security.txt signature, Expires field, and Contact reachability are not verified.
One request from one network vantage point; other regions, clients, and times can differ.
